assessment: Unused reserved time, concentrated requests, unknown equipment needs and inconsistent records leave several plausible explanations for unmet needs. Existing observations do not establish that usable capacity is sufficient. Feasibility and administration cost must be checked against all eight-week targets.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: replacing inherited repeating times with assignments based on stated acceptable windows, required duration and equipment can meet more rehearsal needs within existing capacity.
openings.delta: Contact each group briefly by telephone or in person, record its actual needs, and construct a proposed eight-week schedule. Protect the two performances and each requesting group's weekly 60-minute minimum before distributing remaining time; count that minimum as full satisfaction only when it meets the group's stated need.
openings.prediction: If inherited assignments cause avoidable exclusion, the proposed schedule will satisfy more stated needs than the current schedule using the same rooms, equipment and staffed hours. If acceptable windows and equipment requirements remain incompatible, reassignment alone will fail.
openings.probe: Compare current and proposed schedules against the same recorded needs, including piano requirements and protected events. Check every weekly minimum before implementation; then measure fulfilled needs, conflicts and total administration across eight weeks.
assumptions: Groups can state usable windows and duration needs.
Enough mutually compatible capacity exists for a feasible schedule; this remains unverified.
Groups will accept changed times within their stated windows.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: recording each reservation or change once in an authoritative desk ledger, then confirming its room, date and time to the group, will reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Continue telephone and in-person requests. Give bookings identifiers; record changes against those identifiers, confirm by read-back, and update the online copy from the ledger. Key handover uses the ledger. Treat this as a proposed workflow, not an established explanation of every conflict.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreements and differing booking expectations should decline; administration could improve through fewer corrections or worsen through confirmation work.
openings.probe: During eight weeks, tally disagreements, access conflicts, correction time and all administration minutes, including setup. Inspect whether each conflict originated in inconsistent records or had another cause. Require fewer than two conflicts and an administration average of at most 120 minutes weekly while retaining minimum slots and performances.
assumptions: Desk staff and the volunteer can consistently consult the same ledger.
Confirmation effort fits the administration budget; this requires measurement.
